goal: Merging the version PR publishes the release to npm dist-tag next only; the Claude marketplace plugin source points at the stable branch through git-subdir with ref stable; Antigravity installs from stable; a manual promote workflow fast-forwards stable, tags immune-brain-vX-stable and moves npm latest after validating checklist-mode evidence, and a rollback mode moves both back to the previous -stable tag (Spec D7) (Initiative e2e-release-gate slice S1; Spec docs/specs/e2e-release-gate.spec.md).

acceptance.assertion: The changeset:publish script publishes with --tag next and release.yml contains no step that moves npm latest; .claude-plugin/marketplace.json sets the immune-brain plugin source to {source: git-subdir, url: https://github.com/dereknex/immune-brain.git, path: plugins/immune-brain, ref: stable}. Negative cases: a relative-path source string and a git-subdir source without ref each fail the contract tests. Done looks like: tests/pi-only-release-contract.test.ts and tests/claude-host-package.test.ts assert the next tag and the stable git-subdir source.

scripts/release-promote.ts promote mode, run against a temp Git repository with a bare remote and a stub npm through its --git and --npm seams, fast-forwards stable to the commit tagged immune-brain-vX, creates immune-brain-vX-stable and runs npm dist-tag add immune-brain@X latest; a second run performs no write. Negative cases each refused with a named code before any write: evidence commit differs from the release commit, evidence version differs from X, a checklist item unchecked, immune-brain-vX tag missing, stable not an ancestor of the release commit (non-fast-forward), malformed version string. Done looks like: tests/release-promote.test.ts covers the success, rerun and six refusals.

release-promote.ts --rollback moves stable to the newest immune-brain-v*-stable tag below the current stable commit and sets npm latest to that version; with no previous -stable tag it refuses before any write. Done looks like: tests/release-promote.test.ts covers rollback success and the no-previous-tag refusal.
